brief: c275, promoted. A pane's lamp can go out in the middle of somebody's crossing. `windowLit(sa,sb)` owns bedtime — `windowHours`, HOMES, the miller, the early risers keyed on sunrise — and `paneFigure(sa,sb)` owns the visit, solving `s = (n.t - t0)/(FIG_MIN + FIG_SPAN*hash(...))` over its own window FIG_T0..FIG_T1 clipped to `n.span - 0.8`. Neither asks the other, and `drawPaneFigures` walks LIT_PANES, which is rebuilt each frame from the panes that are lit — so when the lamp goes out under a figure at s = 0.4 the figure does not finish crossing, it ceases. Measure it first (#182's own probe, `probes/pane-figures.mjs`, already reports 1.17 occupied of 13.05 lit and 0 empty nights): count the crossings that are cut short over a seeded year before you fix anything, so the ledger carries the number. Then make the two clocks agree — the cheapest correct fix is for the visit to be offered only inside the lamp's own remaining hours.
successLooksLike: A probe reports the truncation rate on HEAD and 0 after, with occupancy (1.17 of 13.05) and the 52/18/12% at 0/1/2 within noise of #182's numbers — the fix must cost the town almost no figures, and if it costs many, say so and re-price.
avoid: Do not keep a pane lit because somebody is in it — the lamp's clock is the town's bedtime and it wins. Do not give the figure its own persistent object; #182's whole design is that it is solved per frame from `nid` with no anchor that can go stale.
